editorial:
Imagine being stuck between the love of your life and a mother who refuses to let you be happy. That is exactly what happens to Rochus and Judith in this old-school drama. You will feel for Rochus right away because he is just a guy trying to follow his heart, but his mother is a total religious fanatic. She is convinced that her son belongs to the church and not to a girlfriend. The vibe is heavy and full of tension, making you wonder if these two can ever actually find a way to be together or if the pressure will just be too much for them to handle.

What really sticks with you is how the guilt drives the characters toward a sad end. The acting is strong for its time, and the story moves along with a steady, serious pace. While it is a bit slow by today's standards, the emotional payoff is huge. If you enjoy classic stories about forbidden love, you should definitely check this out. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a rainy afternoon when you want a good cry.
endingExplained: The ending is a total heartbreaker. After his mother dies of grief, Rochus feels so guilty that he leaves Judith to become a priest. Judith cannot handle the loss and ends up taking her own life. The most painful part is the final scene where Rochus has to perform the funeral service for the woman he loved. He ends up as a priest, but he loses everything that actually made him happy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old black and white dramas and tragic love stories.
